newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league (kick-off times 1500 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Chelsea (6) v Manchester United (1)

Chelsea are without unsettled striker Gianluca Vialli (bruised foot) as they attempt to complete a premier league double over the leaders. The Italian hit the second goal at Old Trafford last November, but has been restricted mostly to the substitutes' bench by the form of compatriot Gianfranco Zola and Welshman Mark Hughes. Coach Ruud Gullit, who took his team to Italy for a friendly against AC Milan on Wednesday, has welcomed defender David Lee (broken leg) and goalkeeper Dimitri Kharine (knee ligament) back to training and may reshuffle his squad.

United, seeking to avenge that 2-1 home defeat to Chelsea, look for a sixth straight win in defence of their champions' crown. England under-21 midfielder Nicky Butt is out with a swollen ankle, sustained in a 2-1 win at Arsenal on Wednesday. Goalkeeper Peter Scmeichel also has an ankle injury but looks set to play. Frenchman Eric Cantona serves the second match of a two-match ban.
Coventry (16) v Everton (10)

Striker Dion Dublin returns for Coventry after a seven-match ban to add weight to the club's relegation fight which took a blow when they were beaten 2-1 at Aston Villa in midweek. Defender Marcus Hall is expected to play despite a toe injury.

Everton coach Joe Royle is without midfielder Joe Parkinson for a month because of a knee operation. Royle is set to sign Bradford goalkeeper Mark Schwarzer in a week when the club learned their sponsors will withdraw from a 4.0 million pounds ($6.5 million) four-year contract two years early at the end of this season.
Leicester (15) v Derby (12)

Leicester's new signing Robert Ullathorne is out for the remainder of the season with a broken ankle suffered in Tuesday's goalless draw with Wimbledon in the League Cup. Ullathorne was signed from Osasuna in Spain last week to boost the squad for a crowded fixture list as Leicester scrap for survival.

Derby club captain Robin Van der Laan is doubtful with a chest infection after coming off at half-time in the midweek 2-2 draw against Sheffield Wednesday. Striker Ron Willems and defender Jacob Laursen have recovered from hamstring and calf injuries respectively.
Liverpool (2) v Blackburn Rovers (14)

Liverpool crushed Leeds 4-0 in midweek and are bidding to avenge a 3-0 defeat at Blackburn earlier in the season. Coach Roy Evans will select from a fully-fit squad and is likely to field an unchanged team.

Blackburn, knocked out of the F.A. Cup by Coventry last weekend, have lost the form which saw them climb away from the foot of the table. They have won only once in four outings and will hope that Danish international striker Per Pedersen, signed from Odense for 2.5 million pounds ($4 million) on Thursday, will boost their attack. He will start alongside Chris Sutton.
Middlesbrough (20) v Newcastle (4)

In this north-east derby, Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson will be without suspended Brazilian midfielder Emerson. Goalkeeper Gary Walsh (hand) is doubtful and defender Phil Whelan is out (knee). Goalkeeper Alan Miller is back in the squad after recovering from an ankle injury.
Newcastle coach Kenny Dalglish will be missing England midfielder David Batty who begins a two-match ban and defender John Beresford is doubtful with a hamstring problem.
Nottingham Forest (17) v Aston Villa (5)

Forest caretaker player-coach Stuart Pearce was left red-faced after a 1-0 defeat at second division Chesterfield in the fifth round of the F.A. Cup last week. The England defender missed the game through suspension and is out serving the second part of his two-match ban. Midfielder Nigel Clough begins his third month on loan and David Phillips is available after recovering from influenza while defender Colin Cooper becomes captain.
Aston Villa are likely to be unchanged from the side that beat Coventry 2-1 in midweek.
Southampton (19) v Sheffield Wednesday (8)

Southampton manager Graeme Souness will be without midfielder Matthew Oakley (tonsilitis) and Russ Watkinson (chest infection). Defender Francis Benali completes a five-match ban while Richard Dryden begins a two-match ban.

Wednesday manager David Pleat will again be missing midfielder Graham Hyde in an otherwise unchanged squad which drew 2-2 at Derby in midweek, a result which extended their run to one defeat in 19 games.
Sunderland (13) v Leeds (11)

Danish striker Rena Pedersen has joined Sunderland on trial from Belgian club St. Truiden after Peter Reid sent back Cameroon's Alphonse Tchami to Argentine club Boca Juniors. Defender Kevin Ball and midfielder Martin Scott are available for selection after recovering from a fractured jaw and hernia operation respectively.
Leeds manager George Graham is likely to stick with the side that lost 4-0 at Liverpool in midweek.
Arsenal (3) v Wimbledon (7) (Sunday 1600 GMT)

Arsenal coach Arsene Wenger has vowed to sign a striker before the transfer deadline next month after his side suffered a blow to their title aspirations by losing 2-1 to Manchester United in midweek. England defender Tony Adams (ankle) looks set to join fellow international David Seaman on the sidelines for what promises to be a brusing London derby.

Wimbledon coach Joe Kinnear has a fully-fit squad to pick from as he attempts to end a run of three games without a win. Wimbledon, still in two cup competitions as well as pressing for a high league finish, have been rested as they prepare for a spell of congested fixtures.
West Ham (18) v Tottenham Hotspur (9) (Monday 2000 GMT)
Danish defender Marc Rieper is not expected to recover from an ankle injury in time to play as West Ham look to end a run of four games without a win.

Tottenham coach Gerry Francis could recall England striker Teddy Sheringham who has been out with a leg injury since December 28 and 3.2 million pound ($5.2 million) defender John Scales may also return after suffering a hamstring problem.
